## 1. Electron Degeneracy Pressure

When a star exhausts nuclear fuel, gravitational collapse compresses matter to extreme densities $\rho \gtrsim 10^6\text{ g/cm}^3$. In this regime, electrons fill all available phase space cells $(h^3)$ up to the Fermi momentum $p_F$:
$$n_e = \frac{8\pi}{h^3} \int_0^{p_F} p^2 dp = \frac{8\pi}{3h^3} p_F^3 \implies p_F = \left( \frac{3h^3 n_e}{8\pi} \right)^{1/3}$$

### Non-Relativistic Degeneracy ($p_F \ll m_e c$)
The kinetic energy is $E = p^2 / 2m_e$. The resulting electron degeneracy pressure is:
$$P_e = \frac{1}{3} \int_0^{p_F} v p \cdot \frac{8\pi p^2}{h^3} dp = \frac{8\pi}{15 m_e h^3} p_F^5 = \frac{1}{5m_e}\left(\frac{3}{\pi}\right)^{2/3} h^2 n_e^{5/3}$$
Since $n_e = \frac{\rho}{\mu_e m_u}$, this is a polytropic equation of state with index $n = 3/2$ ($\gamma = 5/3$):
$$P \propto \rho^{5/3}$$

Solving the Lane-Emden equation for $n=1.5$ yields the mass-radius relation for non-relativistic white dwarfs:
$$R \propto M^{-1/3}$$
More massive white dwarfs are physically smaller and denser!

---

## 2. Ultra-Relativistic Degeneracy & The Chandrasekhar Limit

As mass increases, density rises until electrons become relativistic ($p_F \gg m_e c$). Then $v \approx c$, and the energy is $E \approx pc$:
$$P_e = \frac{1}{3} \int_0^{p_F} c p \cdot \frac{8\pi p^2}{h^3} dp = \frac{2\pi c}{3 h^3} p_F^4 = \frac{hc}{4}\left(\frac{3}{\pi}\right)^{1/3} n_e^{4/3} \propto \rho^{4/3}$$
This corresponds to a polytrope of index $n = 3$ ($\gamma = 4/3$).

For an $n=3$ polytrope, the radius cancels out completely in the stellar structure mass integral, producing a unique limiting mass:
$$M_{\text{Ch}} = 4\pi \left(\frac{hc}{G}\right)^{3/2} \left(\frac{1}{\mu_e m_u}\right)^2 \omega_3 \approx \frac{5.83}{\mu_e^2} M_\odot$$

For a standard carbon-oxygen white dwarf, $\mu_e \approx 2$, yielding:
$$\boxed{M_{\text{Ch}} \approx 1.44 M_\odot}$$

If the mass of the core exceeds $M_{\text{Ch}}$, electron degeneracy pressure can never halt gravitational collapse, leading inevitably to a neutron star or black hole.
